mainTopic: Canopies inside a סוכה, and whether cutting attached vines (or ציצית strings) counts as 'making' them
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier point: a בית counts as its own tent even under ten טפחים, because it is fixed. The גמרא then brings another version of שמואל's ruling, that a bridal canopy is allowed in the סוכה because it has no roof, and defends it against two ברייתות. One ברייתא is limited to a canopy with a roof. The other is answered by noting that two bed posts (נקליטין) are fixed, so at ten טפחים they make a tent even without a roof. Next, רבה בר רב הונא permits sleeping under any canopy, even one with a roof that is ten טפחים high. He follows רבי יהודה, who holds that a temporary tent does not cancel the סוכה. A new משנה then teaches that attached vines under the סכך make a סוכה unfit unless the vines are cut, and it gives the general rule for valid סכך. The גמרא debates whether cutting the vines is enough. שמואל requires shaking them as well, while רב holds that cutting itself counts as 'making', as he ruled for uncut ציצית strings. The amud ends with a challenge from a ברייתא about ציצית, whose answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A house counts as a tent even under ten handbreadths
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds that a בית, even lower than ten טפחים, is a real אוהל because it is a fixed structure, just like a bed with קינופות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a house too: even if it is not ten handbreadths high, since it is fixed, it is a tent. It is no less than a four-post canopy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the earlier discussion. It adds that a בית, even a very low one, counts as its own tent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a structure needs to be ten טפחים high to count as an אוהל. A בית is different because it is קבוע (fixed and permanent). If even a four-post canopy (קינופות) counts as a tent, then a solid house certainly does.

keyTerms.meaning: A tent (an enclosure that separates you from what is outside it)
Four bed-posts holding a canopy with a flat top
It is no less than (a comparison argument)

phrases.english: And a house too,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין גָּבוֹהַּ עֲשָׂרָה,
phrases.english: even though it is not ten handbreadths high,
since it is fixed,
it is a tent,
phrases.notes: So sleeping inside it does not count as sleeping in the סוכה.

phrases.english: for it is no less than a four-post canopy.
phrases.notes: קינופות count as a tent even when under ten, so a fixed house does too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the first version of the discussion that began on the previous amud.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בית is an אוהל even under ten טפחים, because it is fixed, no less than קינופות.

steps.title: Second version: a bridal canopy is permitted because it has no roof
steps.stepSummary: In another version, רב יהודה quotes שמואל: you may sleep under a כילת חתנים in the סוכה because it has no flat roof, even if it is ten טפחים high.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some report it differently. רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: It is permitted to sleep in a bridal canopy in the סוכה, because it has no roof, even though it is ten handbreadths high.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different version of שמואל's ruling. In this version, what matters is whether the canopy has a roof, not how tall it is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A bridal canopy slopes down from a single pole, so it has no flat top (גג). In this version, a structure without a גג is not a tent, even if it is ten טפחים tall. The next steps will test this idea.

keyTerms.meaning: Another version of the same teaching
A bridal canopy (slopes down from a top pole)
A roof; here, a flat top at least a טפח wide
Ten handbreadths high, the normal height of a tent

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new argument. It is a different report of what שמואל said. In this version the deciding factor is the roof, not the height.

phrases.english: Some say it in another version:
Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
It is permitted to sleep in a bridal canopy in the sukka
because it has no roof,
even though it is ten handbreadths high.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different version of שמואל's ruling than the one just completed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A canopy without a גג is not an אוהל, even if it is ten טפחים high, so one may sleep under it in the סוכה.

steps.title: Challenge: a baraita says sleeping under a canopy does not count
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא: one who sleeps under a כילה in the סוכה has not fulfilled his obligation. This seems to contradict שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: One who sleeps in a canopy in the סוכה has not fulfilled his obligation!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks שמואל's ruling with a ברייתא. The ברייתא says sleeping under a canopy in the סוכה does not count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא mentions no exceptions. It seems to say every canopy blocks the סוכה, which clashes with שמואל, who allows a canopy without a roof.

keyTerms.meaning: They challenged (quoting a תנאי source against an אמורא)
A canopy or net over a bed
He did not fulfill his obligation

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
One who sleeps in a canopy in the sukka
has not fulfilled his obligation!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges שמואל's ruling from step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that a canopy is permitted in the סוכה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says, without any exception, that sleeping under a canopy does not fulfill the מצוה.

steps.title: Answer: the baraita is about a canopy with a roof
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is talking about a canopy that has a flat roof. שמואל only permitted one without a roof.
steps.simpleTranslation: What are we dealing with here? With a case where it has a roof.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends שמואל. It limits the ברייתא to a canopy that has a flat top.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the ברייתא is read as talking about a canopy with a גג, it no longer conflicts with שמואל. A roofed canopy is a tent and blocks the סוכה. A roofless one, like a bridal canopy, does not.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? (used to limit a source to a specific case)

phrases.english: With what are we dealing here?
Where it has a roof.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the source to a specific case (אוקימתא)
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא only forbids a canopy with a גג. שמואל's roofless canopy is still permitted.

steps.title: Second challenge: the baraita about two posts and four posts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא: a sheet over four posts (קינופות) is unfit, while a sheet over two posts (נקליטין) is fit, as long as the posts are not ten טפחים above the bed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: נקליטין are two posts and קינופות are four. If he spread a sheet over the קינופות, it is unfit. Over the נקליטין, it is fit, provided the נקליטין are not ten handbreadths above the bed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a second challenge to שמואל by quoting a ברייתא. The actual inference against שמואל comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Four posts make a flat top, so that canopy is a tent. Two posts hold a single pole, so the sheet slopes and there is no roof. Even so, the ברייתא adds a height condition for the two-post case. That condition is what will cause trouble for שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (introduces a proof or challenge)
Two posts holding a single top pole; the sheet slopes, so there is no roof

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix these up: four posts (קינופות) make a flat roof and are unfit. Two posts (נקליטין) make a slope with no roof and are fit, but only under ten טפחים.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
Naklitin are two posts, and kinofot are four;
if he spread a sheet over the four posts, it is unfit;
over the two posts, it is fit,
provided that the two posts are not
ten handbreadths higher than the bed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first challenge is answered, the גמרא brings a new source against שמואל.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's claim that a roofless canopy is fine even at ten טפחים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא makes the two-post canopy (which has no roof) depend on height. That will be drawn out in the next step.

steps.title: The inference: too tall is unfit even without a roof
steps.stepSummary: From the ברייתא's condition, the גמרא infers that if the two posts are ten טפחים high, the canopy is unfit even though it has no roof. This contradicts שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: This implies that if they are ten handbreadths above the bed, it is unfit, even though it has no roof!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the challenge. It draws an inference from the ברייתא's wording that clashes directly with שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said two posts are fit only when under ten. So at ten they must be unfit, even though a two-post canopy has no roof. שמואל said a roofless canopy is fine even at ten, so the ברייתא appears to contradict him.

keyTerms.meaning: This implies (introduces an inference from a source's wording)

keyTerms.term: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין לָהּ גַּג
keyTerms.meaning: Even though it has no roof

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the roof-based version of שמואל directly against height-based reasoning. The next step (Step 7) resolves it by pointing out that the two posts are fixed.

phrases.aramaic: הָא גְּבוֹהִין מִן הַמִּטָּה עֲשָׂרָה — פְּסוּלָה,
phrases.english: This implies: if they are ten handbreadths above the bed, it is unfit,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין לָהּ גַּג!
phrases.english: even though it has no roof!
phrases.notes: This directly contradicts שמואל's second version.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the inference from the ברייתא quoted in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that a roofless canopy ten טפחים high is permitted
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: From the ברייתא's condition, a roofless two-post canopy becomes unfit at ten טפחים, so height matters even without a roof.

steps.title: Two posts are different because they are fixed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא defends שמואל: the two posts (נקליטין) in the ברייתא are fixed in the bed, unlike a loose bridal canopy, so they can form a tent even without a flat roof.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two posts are different, because they are fixed in place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 6 by showing that the ברייתא's case of two posts is different from שמואל's bridal canopy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל permitted a כילת חתנים because it has no flat roof. The ברייתא's two posts also have no flat roof, but they are firmly attached to the bed. That fixed attachment makes them count as a real tent once they are ten טפחים high, so the ברייתא does not contradict שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: Two posts, one at the head of the bed and one at the foot, with a sheet draped over them
They are fixed / permanently set in place

phrases.english: Two posts are different, because they are fixed.
phrases.notes: The two posts are attached to the bed, unlike a bridal canopy that just hangs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 6 against שמואל.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: the posts are fixed, while the bridal canopy is not.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought that two posts and a bridal canopy are the same, since neither has a flat roof.
steps.terutzMaskana: Two posts are fixed in the bed, so they can make a tent even without a roof. A loose bridal canopy cannot.

steps.title: If the two posts are fixed, treat them like four posts
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer: if two posts are 'fixed', they should be just like four posts (קינופות) and be unfit even below ten טפחים.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they are fixed, let them be like four posts!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer it just gave in Step 7.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said four posts (קינופות) are unfit, with no height condition. It said two posts are fit unless they are ten טפחים high. If two posts are 'fixed' like four posts, why does the ברייתא treat them more leniently?

keyTerms.meaning: Four posts, one at each corner of the bed, with a sheet over them

phrases.english: If they are fixed, let them be like four posts!
phrases.notes: Four posts are unfit even when they are lower than ten טפחים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of Step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in Step 7 that two posts are 'fixed'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'fixed' is the reason, two posts should equal four posts and be unfit at any height. But the ברייתא gives two posts a ten-טפחים condition.

steps.title: Fixed compared to a canopy, but not compared to four posts
steps.stepSummary: Two posts are in the middle: less fixed than four posts, but more fixed than a hanging canopy.
steps.simpleTranslation: Compared to four posts, they are not fixed. Compared to a canopy, they are fixed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by explaining that 'fixed' is a relative term.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two posts are not as solid as four posts, so they only make a tent once they reach ten טפחים. But they are much more solid than a loose כילה, so at ten טפחים they make a tent even without a flat roof. This explains both the ברייתא and שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: A canopy or netting hung over a bed

steps.whatToRemember: Four posts are unfit at any height. Two posts are unfit only from ten טפחים, even without a roof. A loose bridal canopy with no flat roof is fit even at ten טפחים (שמואל).

phrases.english: Compared to four posts, they are not fixed;
compared to a canopy, they are fixed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 8 and closes the defense of שמואל.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Relative definition: being 'fixed' depends on what you compare it to.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Something is either fixed or not fixed, so two posts must be exactly like four posts.
steps.terutzMaskana: Two posts are a middle level. They are less fixed than four posts, which explains the ten-טפחים condition. They are more fixed than a canopy, so they are unfit at ten טפחים even without a roof.

steps.title: Sleeping under a canopy is allowed even with a roof and ten טפחים
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר רב הונא publicly taught that you may sleep under a כילה in the סוכה even if it has a roof and is ten טפחים high.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר רב הונא taught: It is permitted to sleep in a canopy, even if it has a roof, and even if it is ten טפחים high.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new, very lenient teaching from רבה בר רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now, a canopy with a flat roof that is ten טפחים high was considered a separate tent that blocks the סוכה. רבה בר רב הונא permits even that case. The גמרא will now ask which opinion this ruling follows.

phrases.english: Rabba bar Rav Huna taught:
It is permitted to sleep in a canopy,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לָהּ גַּג,
phrases.english: even though it has a roof,
even though it is ten handbreadths high.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new teaching that is more lenient than everything discussed before.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One may sleep under a כילה in the סוכה even if it has a roof and is ten טפחים high.
steps.whyThisMatters: This seems to clash with the ברייתא in Step 3, which (as explained in Step 4) disqualifies a canopy with a roof. The next steps explain that רבה בר רב הונא follows רבי יהודה's principle.

steps.title: This ruling follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whose view רבה בר רב הונא follows and answers: רבי יהודה, who says a temporary tent does not cancel a permanent tent.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? It follows רבי יהודה, who said: a temporary tent does not come and cancel a permanent tent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks itself which opinion the ruling follows and answers right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's principle is that a flimsy, temporary structure like a canopy (אהל עראי) is not strong enough to cancel the סוכה, which is the 'permanent' tent (אהל קבע) for the holiday. So even a roofed canopy does not block the סוכה. The ברייתא that disqualified a roofed canopy follows the רבנן, who disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: Like whom? (Whose opinion does this follow?)
A temporary tent, like a canopy or a bed
A permanent tent; here, the סוכה

steps.confusionAlert: Here the סוכה itself is called the 'permanent tent' (אהל קבע), even though a סוכה is normally a temporary dwelling. The point is only that the סוכה is more permanent than a canopy.

phrases.english: In accordance with whom?
In accordance with Rabbi Yehuda, who said:
A temporary tent does not come
and cancel a permanent tent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies the source for the ruling in Step 10.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא's view does רבה בר רב הונא's ruling follow?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהודה, who holds that a temporary tent does not cancel a permanent tent.

steps.title: Proof: רבי יהודה slept under a bed in the סוכה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה where רבי יהודה reports that they used to sleep under a bed in the presence of the Elders.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: רבי יהודה said, We used to sleep under the bed in front of the Elders.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source showing that רבי יהודה holds a temporary tent does not cancel the סוכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A bed is a temporary structure. If sleeping under it in the סוכה was acceptable, and the Elders saw this and did not object, then the bed did not cancel the סוכה. This is the basis of רבי יהודה's principle.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
In front of the Elders, who saw it and did not object

phrases.english: As we learned: Rabbi Yehuda said:
We were accustomed to sleep beneath the bed
in the presence of the Elders.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the משנה behind רבי יהודה's principle from Step 11.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהודה's view that a temporary tent does not cancel the סוכה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in which רבי יהודה describes sleeping under a bed in the סוכה in front of the Elders.

steps.title: Why not just say the הלכה follows רבי יהודה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבה בר רב הונא gave a specific ruling instead of simply saying the הלכה follows רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let him say: the הלכה follows רבי יהודה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the way רבה בר רב הונא worded his teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If his ruling is just an application of רבי יהודה's view, it would be shorter and clearer to say 'the הלכה follows רבי יהודה'. The גמרא wants to know what his longer wording adds.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law follows רבי יהודה

phrases.english: Then let him say: the halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording of the ruling in Step 10, now that we know it follows רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה בר רב הונא's choice of wording.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A general statement that the הלכה follows רבי יהודה would cover this case, so the specific ruling seems unnecessary.

steps.title: A canopy is like a bed: no difference
steps.stepSummary: Saying only 'the הלכה follows רבי יהודה' could suggest it applies only to a bed. The specific ruling teaches that a canopy is the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he had said 'the הלכה follows רבי יהודה', I would have thought: that applies only to a bed, which is made to be used on top of it. But a canopy, which is made to be used inside it, would not be included. So he teaches us that רבי יהודה's reason is that a temporary tent does not cancel a permanent tent, and a bed and a canopy are the same.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what the specific wording of רבה בר רב הונא adds beyond a general ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A bed is meant to be used on top, so the space underneath might not count as a 'tent' at all. A canopy is meant to be used inside, so it might count as a real tent even according to רבי יהודה. רבה בר רב הונא teaches that רבי יהודה's reason is the temporary-versus-permanent principle, so the canopy is also allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have thought (a mistaken first assumption)
These words apply only to (a limitation)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יהודה, any temporary structure in the סוכה, whether a bed or a roofed canopy, does not cancel the סוכה. רבה בר רב הונא rules this way explicitly so we do not limit it to a bed.

phrases.english: If he had said the halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda,
I would have said:
this applies only to a bed, which is made for use on top of it,
but a canopy, which is made for use inside it,
say that it does not.
So he teaches us
that the reason of Rabbi Yehuda
is that a temporary tent does not come
and cancel a permanent tent,
no difference whether a bed
or a canopy.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי אָמַר הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה, הֲוָה אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording challenge of Step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains what the specific wording adds: it rules out limiting רבי יהודה to a bed.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה might permit only a bed, which is used on top, but not a canopy, which is used inside.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יהודה's reason is that a temporary tent cannot cancel a permanent tent, so a canopy is permitted just like a bed.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to רבה בר רב הונא, following רבי יהודה, one may sleep in the סוכה under a canopy even if it has a roof and is ten טפחים high.

steps.title: Vines growing over the סוכה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a סוכה covered with attached climbing plants plus סכך on top is פסולה, unless the סכך is the majority or the plants are cut.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If someone trained a grapevine, a gourd plant, or ivy over a סוכה and then put סכך on top, the סוכה is unfit. If there was more סכך than plants, or if he cut the plants, it is fit.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It discusses plants that grow over a סוכה while still attached to the ground.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Something still attached to the ground cannot be סכך. So the attached vines spoil the סוכה. There are two fixes: the valid סכך outweighs the vines, or the vines are cut so they are no longer attached.

keyTerms.meaning: He trained a climbing plant upward, like on a trellis
He cut them (detached them from the ground)

steps.confusionAlert: Note the words 'או שקצצן — כשרה'. The גמרא is about to ask whether cutting alone is enough or whether more action is needed.

phrases.english: MISHNA
If one trellised a grapevine over it (the sukkah)
or a gourd plant, or ivy
and then roofed on top of them, it is unfit.
phrases.notes: The plants are still attached to the ground.

phrases.english: But if the roofing was more than them,
or if he cut them, it is fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New משנה that opens a new topic after the כילה discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Attached plants under סכך make the סוכה פסולה, unless the valid סכך is the majority or the plants are cut.

steps.title: The general rule for valid roofing
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives a principle: valid סכך must grow from the ground and must not be מקבל טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is the rule: anything that can become impure or does not grow from the ground may not be used for סכך. Anything that cannot become impure and does grow from the ground may be used for סכך.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה sums up the laws of סכך with one general rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Valid סכך needs two qualities: it grows from the ground, and it is not מקבל טומאה. Vessels fail because they can become impure. Animal hides fail because they do not grow from the ground.

keyTerms.meaning: We may use it as סכך

steps.whatToRemember: Valid סכך = grows from the ground + not מקבל טומאה. Both are required.
steps.confusionAlert: The text reads 'ואין גידולו', which looks like 'and'. It works as 'or': failing either condition is enough to make it invalid.

phrases.english: This is the principle:
Anything that is susceptible to ritual impurity
or whose growth is not from the ground,
one may not roof with it.
And anything that is not susceptible to impurity
and whose growth is from the ground,
one may roof with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with a general principle that covers the vine case and more.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Valid סכך must grow from the ground and must not be מקבל טומאה.

steps.title: Cutting is not enough; the branches must be shaken
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף quotes the משנה's 'cut them — fit' and adds רב's ruling: you must also shake the branches.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רב יוסף sat before רב הונא and said: 'Or if he cut them, it is fit.' And רב said: one must shake them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with רב יוסף adding a condition to the משנה. He says, in רב's name, that after cutting you must also move the branches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the vines grew over the סוכה, they were invalid. Cutting them makes them valid, but they 'became' סכך by themselves without any new action. Because of תעשה ולא מן העשוי (you must make the סוכה, not use something already made), you need a real act, like shaking the branches.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmudic discussion of the משנה
Make it, not from what is already made (the underlying principle)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the whole debate: is detaching the plant itself enough of a 'making', or is a further action needed?

phrases.english: GEMARA

phrases.aramaic: יָתֵיב רַב יוֹסֵף קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא,
phrases.english: Rav Yosef sat before Rav Huna,
and he sat and said:
'Or if he cut them, it is fit,'
and Rav said: one must shake them.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָתֵיב רַב יוֹסֵף קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Qualifies the משנה's ruling that cutting makes the סוכה כשרה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רב (as רב יוסף reports), after cutting the vines one must also shake them.

steps.title: רב הונא corrects who said it
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא tells רב יוסף that this ruling was said by שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said to him: שמואל said this.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא challenges the name רב יוסף attached to the ruling. He says it belongs to שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא is not arguing with the ruling itself. He is objecting to calling it רב's opinion. At this point it is unclear whether he means 'שמואל also said it' or 'only שמואל said it'. Step 20 makes clear that he means only שמואל.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said to him:
Shmuel said this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges who said the ruling in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רב said 'צריך לנענע'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ruling is known in the name of שמואל, so naming רב is questionable.

steps.title: רב יוסף: both of them said it
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף turns away in frustration and answers that both רב and שמואל said it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף turned his face away and said to him: Did I tell you שמואל did not say it? רב said it, and שמואל said it too!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף defends his quote. He took רב הונא's remark as a challenge to his quoting רב, and he answers that שמואל saying it does not contradict him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף takes רב הונא's remark as an objection, as if naming רב meant denying that שמואל said it, and he is annoyed by it. So he answers: there is no conflict, because both אמוראים hold this view.

keyTerms.meaning: He turned his face away (in annoyance)
Did I really say to you...?

phrases.english: Rav Yosef turned his face away
and said to him:
Did I say to you
that Shmuel did not say it?
Rav said it, and Shmuel said it!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַטּוּ מִי קָאָמֵינָא לָךְ דְּלָא אַמְרַהּ שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב הונא's correction in step 18.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב הונא's remark means the ruling cannot be רב's.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both רב and שמואל said it, so naming רב is fine.

steps.title: Only שמואל said it; רב allows cutting alone
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא explains that he meant only שמואל holds this. רב holds that cutting alone makes the סוכה כשרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said to him: This is what I meant: שמואל said it and not רב, because רב rules it fit (by cutting alone).
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא clarifies his point and rejects רב יוסף's answer. רב actually disagrees with the shaking requirement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is now a real disagreement. For שמואל, cutting is not a 'making', so you must shake the branches. For רב, cutting itself counts as the making, so the סוכה is כשרה right away.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what I am telling you

steps.whyThisMatters: It turns a dispute about who said it into a dispute about the law: does detaching count as תעשה?

phrases.english: Rav Huna said to him:
This is what I am saying to you:
that Shmuel said it and not Rav,
because Rav deems it fit.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמֵינָא לָךְ דִּשְׁמוּאֵל אַמְרַהּ וְלָא רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב יוסף's answer that both said it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that רב also requires shaking.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב holds the opposite: cutting alone makes the סוכה כשרה.

steps.title: The story of רב עמרם and the uncut ציצית
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא begins a proof from רב עמרם חסידא, who attached ציצית to his household's garments without first cutting the ends of the strings.
steps.simpleTranslation: As in the case where רב עמרם חסידא put ציצית on the garments of his household members. He attached them but did not cut the ends of their strings.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא starts a story to prove that רב allows cutting alone. The story continues next, so this step is setting up the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Folding long strings in and cutting them afterward raises the same question of תעשה ולא מן העשוי: the ציצית became valid only through cutting. How רב rules on this case will show his view that cutting itself counts as the 'making'.
steps.confusionAlert: The proof is not complete yet. The ruling that comes from this story appears in Step 22, and the lesson is drawn in Step 23.

phrases.english: As in that case where Rav Amram the Pious
cast sky-blue (ritual fringes)
upon the garment of the people of his household.
He attached them, but did not cut
the ends of their strands.
phrases.notes: He looped long strings through and would cut them only afterward.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the proof for רב הונא's claim in step 20 that רב allows cutting alone.
steps.raayaObject: That רב holds cutting itself counts as the 'making' (no further action is needed).
steps.raayaSupportSource: The incident of רב עמרם חסידא's uncut ציצית, which continues next.

steps.title: רב עמרם's question gets רב's answer: just cut them
steps.stepSummary: רב עמרם חסידא brings his question about the uncut ציצית strings to רב חייא בר אשי. He is told in רב's name that he only needs to cut them, and they are כשרות.
steps.simpleTranslation: He came before רב חייא בר אשי. He said to him: This is what רב said: One cuts them apart, and they are fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The story of רב עמרם חסידא continues. He asks about his ציצית and is told that רב rules: just cut the strings now, and the ציצית are fine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב עמרם had hung ציצית on his household's garments while the strings were still joined together in loops, without cutting them first. The worry is that you must 'make' ציצית properly, not just end up with them. רב says cutting them now is enough, and there is no need to take them off and re-tie them.

phrases.aramaic: אֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי,
phrases.english: He (Rav Amram) came before Rav Chiyya bar Ashi,
phrases.notes: רב עמרם חסידא brings his ציצית question to a student of רב.

phrases.english: He said to him: This is what Rav said:
One cuts them apart, and they are fit.
phrases.notes: No need to remove the strings and re-tie them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲתָא לְקַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story begun in Step 21 by giving רב's ruling on רב עמרם's ציצית.
steps.raayaObject: רב הונא's claim (Step 20) that רב holds cutting alone is enough
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב's ruling, reported by רב חייא בר אשי, that ציצית strung joined together become כשרות just by cutting them

steps.title: The lesson: cutting counts as making, for ציצית and for סכך
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws the inference. For רב, cutting the ציצית counts as making them, so cutting the attached vines over the סוכה also counts as making the סכך.
steps.simpleTranslation: So we see: their cutting is their making. Here too: their cutting is their making.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws the point from the story. For רב, the act of cutting counts as making, and the same applies to cutting the attached vines over the סוכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem in both cases is 'תעשה ולא מן העשוי': you must actively make the item, and you cannot just leave it as it already was. רב treats cutting as a real action of making. That proves רב הונא's point that רב does not also require shaking (נענוע) the cut vines.

keyTerms.meaning: Their cutting (detaching the vines from the ground, for סכך)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב, cutting by itself counts as 'making' (עשייה). That is true for ציצית and for סכך. For רב, shaking the cut vines is not needed.

phrases.english: Apparently: their cutting is their making.

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא נָמֵי: קְצִיצָתָן זוֹ הִיא עֲשִׂיָּיתָן.
phrases.english: Here too: their cutting is their making.
phrases.notes: Applied to the vines cut from the ground over the סוכה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the general principle from רב's ציצית ruling and applies it to סכך.
steps.raayaObject: That רב holds cutting the vines alone makes the סכך כשר
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב's ציצית ruling: פסיקתן זו היא עשייתן

steps.title: Does שמואל really disagree? His own teaching suggests cutting is enough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim that שמואל rejects 'cutting is making'. שמואל himself taught a ברייתא saying that strings strung across two corners at once and cut afterward are כשרות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does שמואל really hold that we do not say 'their cutting is their making'? But שמואל taught in the name of רבי חייא: If one strung strings onto two corners at once, and afterward cut the ends of their strings, they are fit. Doesn't it mean that he tied them and then cut them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב הונא's claim that שמואל disagrees with רב. It quotes a teaching from שמואל himself that seems to say cutting after tying is fine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, one long string runs through both corners, so the two sets of ציצית are joined. They are cut apart only at the end. If that means he tied first and cut afterward, then the cutting is what turned them into proper ציצית. That would mean שמואל also holds 'cutting is making'.

keyTerms.meaning: Doesn't it mean...? (pushes for a reading)

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'שתי קרנות בבת אחת' means one continuous string running through both corners. The ציצית on the two corners are physically joined until they are cut. It does not mean two separate ציצית made at the same moment.

phrases.english: And does Shmuel hold that we do not say
phrases.notes: Questioning רב הונא's claim from Step 20.

phrases.english: 'their cutting is their making'?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא תָּנֵי שְׁמוּאֵל מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי חִיָּיא:
phrases.english: But didn't Shmuel teach in the name of Rabbi Chiyya:
If one strung strings onto two corners at once,
phrases.notes: One long string looped through both corners.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַחַר כָּךְ פָּסַק רָאשֵׁי חוּטִין שֶׁלָּהֶן — כְּשֵׁרִין.
phrases.english: and afterward cut the ends of their strings, they are fit.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי לָאו — שֶׁקּוֹשֵׁר וְאַחַר כָּךְ פּוֹסֵק!
phrases.english: Doesn't it mean that he ties and afterward cuts!
phrases.notes: If so, cutting is what makes them proper, which supports 'cutting is making'.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסָבַר שְׁמוּאֵל לָא אָמְרִינַן פְּסִיקָתָן זוֹ הִיא עֲשִׂיָּיתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from רב's view to challenge the claim that שמואל disagrees.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's claim that שמואל does not accept 'פסיקתן זו היא עשייתן'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל's own ברייתא approves ציצית that become separate only by cutting after tying. That suggests שמואל agrees that cutting counts as making.

steps.title: No, the ברייתא means he cut first and then tied
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the ברייתא differently. The strings were cut apart first and only then tied. So the ברייתא does not prove that cutting counts as making.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it means that he cuts and afterward ties.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by reading the ברייתא another way. The cutting came before the tying, so the tying is the real 'making'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the strings were cut apart before tying, the tying itself is the act of making, done to separate ציצית. Then the ברייתא says nothing about whether cutting alone counts as making. שמואל can still hold that it does not.

phrases.english: No, it means that he cuts and afterward ties.
phrases.notes: The order is reversed, so the tying is the act of making.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 24's challenge by rereading the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the source (changing the order of the actions)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא means he tied first and then cut, which would prove that cutting is making.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא means he cut first and then tied, so it proves nothing about cutting alone.

steps.title: But then why teach something so obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the new reading. If he cut the strings first and then tied them, that is the normal way to make ציצית. Why would the ברייתא need to say it?
steps.simpleTranslation: If he cuts and afterward ties, what is the point of saying it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks its own answer. Cutting first and then tying is the ordinary way to make ציצית, so there seems to be no new lesson.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ברייתא is expected to teach something new. Reading it as describing the standard way of making ציצית seems to leave it with nothing to teach. That weakens the answer in Step 25.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the point of saying it? (it seems obvious)

phrases.aramaic: פּוֹסֵק וְאַחַר כָּךְ קוֹשֵׁר מַאי לְמֵימְרָא!
phrases.english: If he cuts and afterward ties, what is the point of saying it!
phrases.notes: That is simply the normal way to make ציצית.

steps.triggerLanguage: פּוֹסֵק וְאַחַר כָּךְ קוֹשֵׁר מַאי לְמֵימְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading offered in Step 25.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of the ברייתא as 'cuts first, then ties'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: On that reading the ברייתא states the obvious standard procedure, and a ברייתא should not be needed for that.

steps.title: Setting up the answer: 'You might have thought…'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins its answer with 'מהו דתימא', which means 'you might have said'. It is about to explain the mistaken idea the ברייתא comes to rule out.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is starting to explain why the ברייתא was needed, and the full answer continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'מהו דתימא' introduces a mistaken assumption a person might have made. The ברייתא was taught to correct that mistake. That gives the ברייתא a real new lesson even if he cut first and then tied.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (introduces a mistaken idea the source comes to reject)

phrases.english: You might have said:
phrases.notes: The answer continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to Step 26's 'what is the point of saying it'.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing a new lesson by naming a mistaken assumption (מהו דתימא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seems to teach nothing new.
steps.terutzMaskana: It comes to reject a possible mistaken idea (spelled out on the next amud).
